questions.note: At ~0.96 px/mm in the full view (1855 mm over ~1785 px) the stature, segment lengths and shoulder-to-crotch (~665 mm) are believable and match the reference apart from the declared leg lengths. Head reads slightly small (~215 mm vertex to chin) on a thick neck, and the right shoulder sits higher and ~50 px wider than drawn because of the pauldron.

Onion shows feet, elbows, stock and muzzle within a few tens of px of the reference; the stance and arm angles match well. Off: the right shoulder/pauldron bulges past the drawn outline, the head faces nearly straight on instead of turned up toward his left, and the torso is a touch more upright and boxy.

Every item is present and roughly where drawn: gaiter, carrier with three-mag placard, antenna at the left shoulder, pauldrons, arm bands, forearm guards, gloves, belt, drop-leg pouches, knee pads over the patellae, boots. Sizes are plausible (mag pouches ~80x165 mm, pads ~140x200 mm). The right forearm guard is oversized and an odd rear belt item juts out.

No visible interpenetration and the carbine stays clear of body and kit, but several hard pieces do not rest on what is under them: the right pauldron stands off the deltoid as a flat board, the arm bands are rigid rings proud of the sleeve, the right forearm guard flares open well clear of the wrist, and a rear belt item's top sticks out from the hip.

Bulk is unevenly distributed: the trousers are skin-tight over the crotch and seat while the shins balloon; sleeves are smooth balloons; the carrier reads as a thin flat plate with little of the reference's chunky shingled load; the armour pieces are flat slabs with no moulded thickness. The man under it reads stockier and softer than the lean reference.

A believable low-ready: right hand on the pistol grip with the index finger indexed along the receiver, left hand overhand on the handguard, muzzle down toward the left knee as drawn, stock up by the right chest. The left hand drapes over the top rather than cradling from below as drawn, and the stock is not anchored against the body or arm.

defects.what: The trousers cling to the groin as a smooth tight V, like tights, while the lower legs are loose and bunched.
defects.fix: G3-class trousers have a gusseted crotch with ease: the fabric should bridge the crotch with a loose fold, not wrap the anatomy.

defects.what: The trouser seat is shrink-wrapped to each buttock and shows the gluteal cleft.
defects.fix: Combat trousers hang from the waist and bridge the cleft with a stretch seat panel; drape the seat with more ease or a gusset.

defects.what: The right forearm guard is a rigid drum whose wrist end flares open far wider than the wrist, leaving a visible ring of air around the glove cuff.
defects.fix: Real forearm guards are curved shells strapped close to the forearm, tapering toward the wrist and sitting on the sleeve.

defects.what: The upper-arm bands are stiff hard rings that stand proud of the sleeve on the outer side instead of cinching it.
defects.fix: A strap or articulated lame bears on the sleeve: compress the cloth under it and let the band follow the arm's taper.

defects.what: The right pauldron is a flat planar board tilted outward, standing off the deltoid and widening the shoulder beyond the drawn outline.
defects.fix: Shoulder armour is moulded to the deltoid curve and hangs from the carrier strap, lying on the sleeve.

defects.what: The pauldron edges are ragged and stepped, like stacked torn sheets, on both shoulders at the head zoom.
defects.fix: Moulded armour has a clean continuous edge, often with a rolled lip or binding.

defects.what: The right boot's lower is a seamless smooth rubber shell with lacing only from the upper instep: it reads as a duck boot, not a Zephyr-class boot.
defects.fix: Zephyr-class boots lace from near the toe, with a rubber toe rand and separate suede/textile panels stitched over the vamp and quarters.

defects.what: A rear belt item behind the right hip has its top piece angled ~40 degrees away from the body, reading as a lid stuck open or a part not attached.
defects.fix: Pouch lids and sheath tops close flat against the body; attach the item to the belt with its top tight to the hip.

defects.what: The left elbow pad is a small ball stuck on the elbow with no visible straps or wrap.
defects.fix: Elbow pads are curved caps that wrap the olecranon, held by elastic straps above and below the joint.

defects.what: The knee pads are flat bevelled slabs with a planar face, not domed caps.
defects.fix: AirFlex-class pads have a domed, articulated cap over the patella with a moulded rim.

defects.what: The carrier front reads as a thin plain flat plate with a small placard; the reference's chunky carrier with shingled admin panel and padded straps has lost its bulk.
defects.fix: A loaded JPC-class front carries a ~25 mm plate in a padded bag plus admin and mag pouches standing 50-70 mm off the chest.

defects.what: The head faces nearly straight to camera; the reference turns it toward his left and slightly up.
defects.fix: Turn the head toward his left and lift the chin to match the drawn gaze.

defects.what: The hard armour (pauldrons, bands, forearm guards, knee pads) is a light, cool, glossy grey; the reference's is dark worn olive-tan.
defects.fix: Darker olive-tan polymer with edge wear and grime, near the carrier's value.

defects.what: The sleeves read as smooth inflated balloons over the upper arms, losing the fitted combat shirt shape.
defects.fix: A combat shirt sleeve fits close over the biceps and deltoid with a few draped folds.

ranked: [D1] The trousers wrap the crotch like tights while the shins hang loose and bunched; no tailor cuts G3-class trousers that way, and it is the first thing that reads wrong in the clay.
[D2] From behind the seat is shrink-wrapped to each buttock with the cleft showing; real combat trousers bridge it.
[D13] The hard armour is light cool glossy grey plastic; against the reference's dark worn olive-tan it looks like a toy and breaks the kit's unity of value.
[D5] The right pauldron is a flat board tilted off the shoulder rather than a shell moulded to the deltoid, and it widens his right shoulder past the drawn outline.
[D3] The right forearm guard is an oversized drum flaring open around the wrist with air all round the glove cuff; a real guard straps close and tapers.
[D7] The boots read as duck boots: a seamless rubber lower and laces only from the instep, where a Zephyr-class boot laces near the toe over stitched panels with a rand.
[D11] The carrier has lost its mass: a thin plain front plate and small placard instead of the reference's chunky padded carrier and stacked pouches.
[D4] The upper-arm bands are rigid rings standing proud of the sleeve; a strap or lame would bear on and dent the cloth.
[D8] A rear belt item behind the right hip has its top angled ~40 degrees off the body, like an open lid or an unattached part.
[D12] The head looks straight at camera; the reference turns it toward his left and up, which changes the read of the whole pose.
[D14] Sleeves are smooth balloons with no fitted combat-shirt shape, which makes the arms soft and heavy.

The left hand lies overhand on top of the handguard and the stock floats by the chest unanchored; a believable hold, but looser than the drawn one where the hand cradles from below and the stock rides the shoulder pocket.
[D10] The knee pads are flat bevelled slabs; real pads have a domed cap over the patella.
[D9] The left elbow pad is a little ball on the elbow, with no wrap or straps.
[D6] At the head zoom the pauldron edges are ragged and stepped like stacked torn sheets.
The gloves are smooth rubbery mitts with uniform thick fingers; the reference's are knuckled impact gloves.
Outside scope but spoiling identity: the hair is a hard cap with a straight edge high across the forehead and spikes on top.
